Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{LM}$ in terms of $\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the leg $\overset{―}{MN}$ opposite the given angle $m∠L$  and wish to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{LM}.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the hypotenuse is *sine*. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(m∠L) & =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{6}{LM} \\ LM\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =6 \\ LM & =\frac{6}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$
